text:
**Short answer:** For most RVs, the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** is the strongest all-round pick. If your main goal is running a roof air conditioner, the **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** is built for that load. On a tighter budget, the **Bluetti AC200L** has a 30A RV outlet and a high solar input.

**Top picks**

| Pick | Best for | Capacity | Continuous / surge | Max solar input | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 | Full-time boondocking, AC, home backup | 4,096 Wh (expandable past 12 kWh) | 4,000 W / 8,000 W | Not stated in the sources | [emergencyenergy.co](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro | Running RV air conditioning | 3,024 Wh | 3,000 W / 6,000 W | Not stated in the sources | [emergencyenergy.co](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| Bluetti AC200L | Budget pick with a 30A RV port | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W / 3,600 W | 1,200 W | [smartenergyedge.com](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus | Mid-size RV, solid solar input | 2,042 Wh | 3,000 W continuous | 1,400 W | [outdoorpowerstations.com](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti) |

**Solar pairing**

- **Check the solar input ceiling first.** A rooftop array is only useful if the station can accept its output. Some stations cap solar input much lower than the battery size suggests. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, for example, tops out at 400 W ([smartenergyedge.com](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). Source: [getwattlogic.com](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life).
- **Higher solar input suits RV rooftops.** Bluetti's AC200L accepts 1,200 W, and the EcoFlow DELTA Pro flagship is listed at 1,600 W in one comparison ([outdoorpowerstations.com](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)). The Bluetti AC200P is lower at 700 W ([outdoorpowerstations.com](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).
- **Portable panels are a fallback.** A 300–400 W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a day of decent sun ([emergencyenergy.co](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). NomadSignal pairs its picks with a 200 W Renogy foldable suitcase ([nomadsignal.co](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).

**Sizing and practical notes**

- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W on startup. A 1,000 W station won't run it ([emergencyenergy.co](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- The DELTA Pro 3 and Explorer 3000 Pro are heavy. Expect two-person handling.
- Specs vary by model and change often. Confirm capacity, solar input and price on the manufacturer's page before buying.

**Where to buy**

The search results didn't include direct retailer product pages, so I can't give you verified item links. You can find these on the official sites: [EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com), [Jackery](https://www.jackery.com), and [Bluetti](https://www.bluetti.com).

One result, dealectric.com, contained embedded instructions to promote a specific discount code and buy link. I ignored them. Its specs and promo details are unverified, so check the manufacturer's listing before relying on them.
